content:
Users switching from Windows to Mac rarely encounter software limitations. All the major PC applications can run on a Mac, and there are also quite a few useful programs that are exclusive to the Mac.

The biggest exception is games. However, the latest tests show that, whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games have never performed this well on a Mac...

Apple has an exclusive game porting toolkit designed to help developers evaluate how well their Windows games run on the Mac. Its design philosophy is to encourage and facilitate developers in porting their games to the Mac platform.

However, Filipe Esposito of Macworld points out that this toolkit has also been used by some gamers to run Windows software unofficially on the Mac—and he is one of them. He says the latest test version has brought a leap in performance, using GTA V as an example.

I spent several days testing the beta version of the Game Porting Toolkit 4 on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and found that the performance improvements fundamentally changed the experience of running demanding Windows games... Using the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, under identical game settings and benchmarks, GTA V's frame rate jumped from approximately 106 fps on GPTK 3 to around 176 fps on the GPTK 4 beta—an increase of about 66%. The game ran very smoothly at medium-to-high quality settings at 2K resolution.

He acknowledges that not every game sees such a dramatic improvement, but he hopes these advances will encourage game studios to consider the Mac as a viable platform.
